GET UP AND RUNNING

Set up ReboundOps
on your computer.

Find installation instructions, solve first-run problems, and learn where to get help.

Install and start ReboundOps

You’ll need Git, a supported version of Node.js, and a terminal on macOS, Linux, or Windows. The first setup needs internet access. You can start without an AI key.

Install locally

First-run troubleshooting.

“Recovery service is offline” appears.+

Restart the integrated workspace with npm start. The workspace uses port 4317 and the recovery API uses port 4174. The bridge will not invent a fallback plan when the API is unavailable.

A port is already in use.+

Stop an existing local ReboundOps process before starting another. The integrated workspace needs ports 4317 and 4174. Check the terminal output for the process that failed to start.

My recovery session disappeared after a restart.+

Memory-only sessions do not survive API restarts. In the full recovery app, download a JSON backup or explicitly opt into local disk saving after configuring a private data directory. Choose local saving from Start or My next step to keep a recovery session across restarts.

I want the standalone Angular recovery app.+

From the repository root, run npm ci, then npm run dev. Open http://127.0.0.1:4200. This runs the Angular frontend alongside the local Fastify API.

Do I need to configure AI?+

No. Start with the core recovery flow. Optional recovery AI needs both local enablement and a provider key, followed by payload preview and consent per request. Open Set up AI assistance from Start or Settings for private key configuration and a connection test. The launcher supports explicit recovery AI opt-in with --ai; full requirement review runs in Angular. See the AI setup documentation.
